Beaverdale's Best: A Local's Guide to Des Moines' Most Charming Brick Streets

Nestled in the heart of Des Moines, Iowa, Beaverdale stands as a testament to the city's rich architectural heritage and small-town charm within an urban setting. This beloved neighborhood, with its iconic brick streets and tree-lined boulevards, offers visitors and residents alike a glimpse into what makes Des Moines one of the Midwest's most livable cities. Whether you're searching for "historic neighborhoods near me" or planning your first visit to Central Iowa, Beaverdale's brick streets tell a story that's been decades in the making.

The History Behind Beaverdale's Iconic Brick Streets

The brick streets of Beaverdale Des Moines aren't just charming—they're a living piece of Iowa history. Laid in the early 1900s, these distinctive red-brick roadways were once the standard for urban development across the Midwest. While most cities paved over their brick streets with asphalt, Beaverdale residents fought to preserve this unique character, making it one of the few Des Moines historic neighborhoods to maintain its original infrastructure.

The neighborhood's development coincided with Des Moines' expansion as a major insurance and financial hub, with companies like Principal Financial establishing their headquarters in the city. As executives and professionals sought comfortable residential areas, Beaverdale emerged as a premier destination, featuring Craftsman bungalows, Tudor revivals, and Colonial homes that still grace these brick-paved streets today.

Why Brick Streets Matter to Beaverdale's Identity

The Beaverdale brick streets serve multiple purposes beyond aesthetics. They naturally slow traffic, creating a pedestrian-friendly environment that encourages walking and community interaction. During Iowa's notoriously hot summers, the brick surface actually helps with water drainage better than traditional asphalt, an important consideration given Central Iowa's spring flooding concerns. These streets have become so integral to the neighborhood's identity that preservation efforts continue to this day, with residents actively participating in maintenance and restoration projects.

Must-See Streets and Blocks in Beaverdale

When exploring the best brick streets in Des Moines, certain blocks in Beaverdale stand out as particularly picturesque and historically significant.

Beaver Avenue: The Heart of the Neighborhood

\p>Beaver Avenue serves as Beaverdale's main commercial corridor, where brick streets meet local businesses that have served the community for generations. This stretch features:

  • Historic storefronts dating back to the 1920s and 1930s
  • Local restaurants and cafes perfect for a post-walk refreshment
  • Specialty shops offering everything from antiques to artisan goods
  • The iconic Beaverdale Brick sign, a popular photo opportunity for visitors

The brick pavement along Beaver Avenue creates a distinctive rumble as cars pass over it—a sound that longtime residents consider the neighborhood's signature soundtrack.

Franklin Avenue's Residential Charm

Franklin Avenue showcases some of the finest examples of early 20th-century residential architecture in the Des Moines area. The brick streets here wind past beautifully maintained homes with expansive front porches, mature oak and maple trees, and gardens that burst with color during Iowa's spring and summer months. This street is particularly stunning during autumn when the tree canopy transforms into a kaleidoscope of reds, oranges, and golds—rivaling even the displays at the nearby Des Moines Art Center.

Urbandale Avenue's Hidden Gems

Connecting Beaverdale to neighboring Urbandale, this brick-paved stretch offers a quieter walking experience. The street features several homes listed on the National Register of Historic Places and provides excellent examples of how Des Moines historic neighborhoods have maintained their character while adapting to modern life.

Best Ways to Experience Beaverdale's Brick Streets

Walking Tours: The Ideal Approach

The best way to appreciate the Beaverdale brick streets is on foot. Create your own self-guided walking tour by starting at the Beaverdale Farmers Market (held seasonally, similar to the popular Downtown Farmers Market). From there, meander through the residential streets, taking time to notice the architectural details that make each home unique.

Insider tip: Visit during early morning or late afternoon for the best lighting for photography and to avoid Iowa's intense midday summer heat.

Cycling Through History

For cycling enthusiasts—especially those who've tackled RAGBRAI—Beaverdale offers a gentler ride through history. The brick streets provide a unique cycling experience, though be prepared for a slightly bumpier ride than the smooth trails at nearby Gray's Lake or the Meredith Trail. Many Drake University students bike through Beaverdale when commuting between campus and other Des Moines neighborhoods.

Seasonal Experiences

Each Iowa season brings a different character to Beaverdale Des Moines:

  • Spring: Blooming gardens and tree blossoms frame the brick streets perfectly
  • Summer: Evening walks reveal neighbors gathering on porches, embodying Midwest hospitality
  • Fall: The brick streets become carpeted with colorful leaves, creating postcard-worthy scenes
  • Winter: Snow-dusted brick streets and holiday decorations transform the neighborhood into a winter wonderland

Local Businesses and Landmarks Along the Brick Streets

Exploring Beaverdale's brick streets isn't complete without stopping at the local establishments that give this Des Moines neighborhood its distinctive character.

Dining and Refreshments

Several beloved local restaurants line the brick streets of Beaverdale, offering everything from casual coffee shops to upscale dining experiences. These establishments embody the farm-to-table ethos that's become central to Des Moines' growing food scene, often sourcing ingredients from Central Iowa farms and producers.

Shopping Local

The brick-paved commercial district features independently owned shops that have resisted the big-box trend. From bookstores to boutiques, these businesses contribute to Beaverdale's reputation as one of the most walkable and community-oriented neighborhoods in the Des Moines area.

Community Gathering Spaces

Beaverdale Park, accessible via the neighborhood's brick streets, serves as a central gathering place for community events throughout the year. The park hosts everything from summer concerts to fall festivals, creating opportunities for visitors to experience authentic Des Moines community culture.

Preservation Efforts and Community Pride

What makes Beaverdale truly special isn't just the brick streets themselves—it's the community's dedication to preserving them. The Beaverdale Neighborhood Association works tirelessly to maintain these historic roadways, organizing fundraisers and coordinating with the City of Des Moines on restoration projects.

This preservation mindset extends beyond the streets to the entire neighborhood character. Residents take pride in maintaining their historic homes, following architectural guidelines that preserve the area's early 20th-century aesthetic while allowing for modern updates. This balance between preservation and progress has made Beaverdale a model for other Des Moines historic neighborhoods like Sherman Hill and the East Village.

How Visitors Can Support Preservation

When visiting Beaverdale Des Moines, you can support preservation efforts by:

  • Shopping at local businesses along the brick streets
  • Attending community events and festivals
  • Respecting residential areas and private property
  • Sharing your experience on social media to promote awareness
  • Considering a donation to the Beaverdale Neighborhood Association

Planning Your Visit to Beaverdale's Brick Streets

Getting There

Beaverdale is located in northwest Des Moines, easily accessible from downtown Des Moines, West Des Moines, and Urbandale. The neighborhood is approximately 10 minutes from the Iowa State Capitol and 15 minutes from Principal Park, making it an easy addition to any Des Moines itinerary.

Best Times to Visit

While the Beaverdale brick streets are beautiful year-round, certain times offer enhanced experiences:

  • May through October: Ideal weather for walking tours and outdoor dining
  • Fall Festival (September): Annual celebration featuring local vendors and entertainment
  • Holiday season: Decorated homes and streets create a festive atmosphere
  • Weekday mornings: Quieter streets perfect for photography and peaceful walks

What to Bring

For the best experience exploring these Des Moines historic neighborhoods, come prepared:

  • Comfortable walking shoes (brick streets can be uneven)
  • Camera or smartphone for capturing architectural details
  • Water bottle, especially during Iowa summers
  • Light jacket for spring and fall visits
  • Reusable shopping bag for local purchases

Beyond the Brick Streets: Exploring Greater Beaverdale

While the brick streets are Beaverdale's signature feature, the neighborhood offers much more to discover. The area connects seamlessly to other Des Moines attractions, making it easy to create a full day of exploration. From Beaverdale, you're just minutes from the Des Moines Art Center, the Science Center of Iowa, and the vibrant Ingersoll Avenue district.

The neighborhood's proximity to Drake University adds a youthful energy, with students and faculty contributing to the area's coffee shop culture and community events. This blend of historic preservation and contemporary vitality makes Beaverdale Des Moines a microcosm of what makes the entire city special—respect for heritage combined with forward-thinking innovation.

Why Beaverdale Matters to Des Moines

In an era of rapid development and urban sprawl, Beaverdale's brick streets represent something increasingly rare: a neighborhood that has maintained its historic character while remaining vibrant and relevant. These streets aren't museum pieces—they're living, functioning parts of a thriving community where families raise children, neighbors know each other by name, and local businesses flourish.

For visitors to Des Moines, Beaverdale offers an authentic glimpse into Midwest neighborhood life that you won't find in guidebooks focused solely on downtown attractions. It's where you'll discover the Iowa values of community, preservation, and quality of life that make Des Moines consistently rank among America's best places to live.

Whether you're a history buff fascinated by urban development, an architecture enthusiast drawn to Craftsman and Tudor homes, or simply someone seeking a pleasant afternoon walk through one of Central Iowa's most charming neighborhoods, the brick streets of Beaverdale Des Moines deliver an experience that's uniquely Iowan and undeniably special.

Ready to explore? Lace up your walking shoes, grab your camera, and discover why locals consider Beaverdale's brick streets one of Des Moines' best-kept secrets. These historic roadways aren't just paths through a neighborhood—they're connections to the past, celebrations of community, and invitations to experience the authentic character that makes Des Moines, Iowa, a destination worth discovering.
